nodes.content: Design an ownership type checker for cancellable asynchronous tasks that safely transfer borrowed resources across task boundaries.
requirements: Guarantee memory safety under cancellation and task migration without whole-program analysis or runtime borrow checks.
Accept 12 safe and reject 12 unsafe programs covering nested borrows, ownership transfer, and cancellation.

nodes.content: Use region-indexed task scopes, linear join obligations, cancellation-shielded child draining, and Send/Sync-qualified transfers for migration.
How can a cancelled parent keep a borrowed resource alive until every child using it has stopped?
A linear join token whose cancellation-safe scope cleanup drains children before resource destruction prevents dangling borrows after parent cancellation.
Define cancellation-safe scope-exit lowering: cancel children, shield joins, then expire region loans; check nested borrows and migration.
Implement ScopeIR’s cancel–shield–join–expire lowering and type-check 24 fixtures covering nested borrows, ownership moves, migration, and cancellation.
ScopeIR checker with cancel–shield–join–expire lowering and 12 expected-safe and 12 expected-unsafe fixtures covering nested borrows, moves, migration, and cancellation.
Run ScopeIR’s 12-safe/12-unsafe suite and enumerate cancellation/migration schedules through four suspension points, checking classification and dangling loans.
ScopeIR accepted 12/12 safe and rejected 12/12 unsafe fixtures; 256 cancellation/migration schedules exposed zero dangling loans.
Retain ScopeIR’s linear joins and cancellation-shielded draining; fixture and schedule results justify this baseline, not a general safety proof.
Mechanize ScopeIR transitions in Lean 4, checking loan liveness under nested reborrows, migration, and cancellation during shielded joins.
Lean 4 found a three-task counterexample: direct-child joins closed an outer loan while a migrated grandchild retained its reborrow.
Transitive, region-indexed join obligations keep loans live until all borrowing descendants drain, even after intermediate-task cancellation or migration.
Extend ScopeIR with region-indexed descendant obligations propagated through spawn and discharged only after cancellation-shielded subtree draining.
Implement compositional region-obligation typing, prove cancellation and migration safety, then rerun 24 fixtures and the grandchild counterexample.
Patch ScopeIR with descendant obligations; compare baseline and revised checkers on 24 fixtures and the migrated-grandchild cancellation trace.
Baseline missed the migrated-grandchild dangling reborrow; revised checker rejected it while preserving 12/12 safe accepts and 12/12 unsafe rejects.
Can region-indexed obligations handle recursive child spawning compositionally without enumerating descendants or analyzing the whole task tree?
Region-polymorphic spawn-effect summaries permit local recursive-call checking while scope-local child registries ensure descendants drain before loan expiry.
Model-check recursive spawn depths 1–8 under cancellation and migration, testing region-polymorphic summaries and transitive obligations for dangling loans.
Across recursive spawn depths 1–8, local summary checking succeeded; 4,096 cancellation/migration traces showed zero dangling loans.
Provisionally adopt transitive obligations and region-polymorphic summaries: 24 fixtures classify correctly, and 4,096 recursive traces show no dangling loans.
Mechanize ScopeIR in Lean 4 and prove loan liveness across atomic spawn registration, shielded subtree draining, and Send/Sync migration.
ScopeIR.lean contains a loan-liveness theorem and typed transition rules for atomic spawn registration, shielded subtree draining, and Send/Sync migration.
Audit ScopeIR.lean with Lean 4 `#print axioms`, replay the migrated-grandchild trace, and inspect cancellation and destructor assumptions.
Audit found no custom axioms or `sorry`; migrated-grandchild replay kept the outer loan live until shielded descendant draining completed.
Compile task scopes into affine cancellation continuations that retain owner frames until supervised child completion, enforcing Send/Sync on migration.
How are owner frames kept alive when cancellation races migration of an affine child continuation?
Run ScopeIR’s 24 fixtures under forced cancel/migrate races at continuation handoff, checking owner frames outlive child completion.
All 24 fixtures classified correctly, but one cancel/migrate handoff schedule freed an owner frame before its child completed.
Atomic registration of affine continuations with the destination supervisor before source release keeps owner frames live across cancel/migrate races.
Model-check atomic supervisor handoff against ScopeIR’s baseline joins across cancel/migrate interleavings, tracking owner-frame lifetime and child completion.
Atomic handoff with transitive joins preserved owner frames across 1,024 cancel/migrate races, reviving scoped joins; direct-child joins still failed.
Adopt transitive scoped joins with atomic supervisor handoff and shielded draining; Lean audit and 1,024 races support modeled safety.
Integrate atomic handoff into ScopeIR lowering, prove supervisor-retention invariants, and rerun 24 fixtures plus adversarial cancellation/migration schedules.
Extend ScopeIR.lean with atomic supervisor-handoff transitions and prove owner-frame retention until every registered descendant completes.
ScopeIR-Handoff.lean adds atomic registration/release transitions and a supervisor-retention lemma covering cancellable, migrating child continuations.
ScopeIR.lean v2 replaces independent migration transitions with atomic supervisor handoff and updates loan-liveness proofs to require owner-frame retention.
Use generative scope brands and affine child permits; drain outstanding permits before cancellation destroys owners, requiring Send-safe migration.
Generative scope brands and transitive affine permits classify 24 fixtures correctly and prevent dangling loans across atomic cancel/migrate handoffs.
Encode branded affine permits in ScopeIR-Handoff.lean; audit its retention lemma and rerun 24 fixtures plus 1,024 cancel/migrate schedules.
Branded permits accepted unsafe U12: atomic cancel/migrate handoff released an owner while its migrated grandchild held a reborrow.
Generative brands and affine permits remain safe if handoff atomically transfers descendant-region obligations and retains owners through acknowledged draining.
Add atomic descendant-obligation transfer and drain acknowledgments, then recheck U12, the 24 fixtures, and formal owner-retention invariants.
Implement atomic descendant-obligation handoff and drain acknowledgments for permits; replay U12, 24 fixtures, and 1,024 cancellation/migration schedules with retention assertions.
Revised permits rejected U12 and all 12 unsafe fixtures, accepted all 12 safe fixtures; 1,024 schedules preserved owner retention.
Keep transitive scoped joins; require atomic descendant-obligation transfer and acknowledged draining for branded permits, because U12 defeated weaker handoff.
How can borrowed child permits be prevented from escaping their generative scope into detached tasks?
Test ScopeIR.lean v2 against detached-spawn, captured-closure, and returned-permit escapes using rank-2 scope-brand nonescape checks.
Replace permit-only lifetime tracking with rank-2 scope-branded borrow types and transitive join effects checked at each spawn.
Can rank-2 branded borrow types block detached-task escapes while allowing nested borrowed children under transitive joins?
Add rank-2 brand nonescape rules, test three detached-escape patterns and nested safe children, then rerun the 24-fixture suite.
Extend ScopeIR.lean v2 with rank-2 brand checks and acknowledged descendant draining; run three escape tests and 24 fixtures.
ScopeIR.lean v3 adds rank-2 scope-brand nonescape rules, atomic descendant-obligation transfer, and acknowledged draining before owner destruction.
Compare ScopeIR.lean v3’s rank-2 checks with permit-only typing on three escapes, nested children, 24 fixtures, and cancel/migrate schedules.
Rank-2 checks rejected three detached escapes accepted by permit-only typing, preserved nested children and 24/24 classifications; 1,024 schedules remained loan-safe.
Adopt rank-2 scope brands with transitive joins and atomic, acknowledged handoff; they block escapes and preserve all 24 fixture classifications.
Prove rank-2 nonescape and nested-child typing preservation in Lean 4, then stress-test higher-order captures and cancellation handoff.
Formalize rank-2 brand substitution and nested-spawn preservation in ScopeIR.lean v3; test closure captures across detached spawns and cancellation.
ScopeIR.lean v4 adds rank-2 brand substitution and nested-spawn preservation lemmas, replacing v3’s unproved nonescape checks.
Audit v4 proof dependencies and replay detached captures plus nested borrowed children under cancellation, checking nonescape and loan liveness.
Lean 4 audit found no `sorry` or custom axioms; detached captures failed typing, while nested borrowed children survived cancellation.
